Include it once, near the top of any `format: live-html` / `engine: jupyter`

at the text level, before HTML comments are stripped, so a literal one here
would make this file include itself.

It imports numpy/matplotlib/climt/sympl and defines
`integrate_to_equilibrium(...)` for the RCE pages. The climt wheel itself is
installed by micropip at document setup via the including page's
`pyodide: packages:` front-matter block (a CORS-served localhost wheel locally;
the GitHub release asset for the published site).

The `integrate_to_equilibrium` body below is duplicated in the natively

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: true
#| edit: false
# The climt wheel is installed by micropip at document setup (before any cell
# runs) via the `pyodide: packages:` block in the page front matter — see
# radiative-transfer/09-live-rce.qmd. Installing here with `await
# micropip.install(...)` instead would race: quarto-live does not await one
# autorun cell's async work before starting the next, so a downstream cell can
# run before the wheel finishes installing. So this cell is synchronous.
import asyncio

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import climt
from sympl import AdamsBashforth
from datetime import timedelta


async def animate_to_equilibrium(tendency_components, state, timestep, n_steps,
                                 redraw_every=20, title=""):
    """Step forward toward radiative equilibrium, live-updating three panels:
    temperature, longwave heating rate, and up/downwelling longwave flux.

    Browser-only (async + matplotlib). The stepping is the same loop, with the
    same update order, as ``integrate_to_equilibrium`` (which the native test
    guards); ``await asyncio.sleep(0)`` yields to the browser so it repaints the
    canvas between redraws — the Pyodide equivalent of ``%matplotlib`` live
    updating. Only tendency components are supported (the RCE demo uses none of
    the stepper kind).
    """
    model = AdamsBashforth(list(tendency_components))
    p = state["air_pressure"].values[:, 0, 0] / 100.0
    p_int = state["air_pressure_on_interface_levels"].values[:, 0, 0] / 100.0

    fig, (ax_t, ax_h, ax_f) = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(11, 4.2), sharey=True)
    (line_t,) = ax_t.plot(state["air_temperature"].values[:, 0, 0], p)
    (line_h,) = ax_h.plot(np.zeros_like(p), p)
    (line_u,) = ax_f.plot(np.zeros_like(p_int), p_int, label="up")
    (line_d,) = ax_f.plot(np.zeros_like(p_int), p_int, label="down")
    ax_t.set_ylabel("pressure (hPa)")
    ax_t.set_xlabel("temperature (K)"); ax_t.set_title("Temperature")
    ax_h.set_xlabel("LW heating (K day$^{-1}$)"); ax_h.set_title("Heating rate")
    ax_f.set_xlabel("LW flux (W m$^{-2}$)"); ax_f.set_title("Up / down flux")
    ax_f.legend(loc="upper right")
    ax_t.invert_yaxis()  # shared y: inverts all three
    for ax in (ax_t, ax_h, ax_f):
        ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    if title:
        fig.suptitle(title)
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

    for i in range(n_steps):
        diagnostics, new_state = model(state, timestep)
        state.update(new_state)
        state.update(diagnostics)
        state["time"] += timestep
        if i % redraw_every == 0 or i == n_steps - 1:
            line_t.set_xdata(state["air_temperature"].values[:, 0, 0])
            line_h.set_xdata(
                state["air_temperature_tendency_from_longwave"].values[:, 0, 0])
            line_u.set_xdata(state["upwelling_longwave_flux_in_air"].values[:, 0, 0])
            line_d.set_xdata(state["downwelling_longwave_flux_in_air"].values[:, 0, 0])
            for ax in (ax_t, ax_h, ax_f):
                ax.relim()
                ax.autoscale_view(scalex=True, scaley=False)
            fig.canvas.draw()
            await asyncio.sleep(0)
    return state


def integrate_to_equilibrium(tendency_components, stepper_components, state,
                             timestep, n_steps):
    """Step tendency + stepper components forward toward radiative equilibrium.

    Keep this body in sync with the copy in
    docs/radiative-transfer/_live/rce_helpers.py.

    Update order matters: the new (prognostic) state is applied *before* the
    diagnostics, so flux diagnostics (e.g. the longwave fluxes SlabSurface
    consumes) survive into the next step instead of being clobbered by the
    stepper carrying those fields forward at their pre-step value.
    """
    model = AdamsBashforth(list(tendency_components))
    for _ in range(n_steps):
        diagnostics, new_state = model(state, timestep)
        state.update(new_state)
        state.update(diagnostics)
        for stepper in stepper_components:
            s_diag, s_new = stepper(state, timestep)
            state.update(s_new)
            state.update(s_diag)
        state["time"] += timestep
    return state


# End on a plain statement (not a def): quarto-live captures each cell's final
# value for display, and marshalling a bare function object through JS interop
# yields an unhashable JsProxy that aborts the cell.
print("climt", climt.__version__, "ready — has_fortran:", climt.has_fortran_extensions())
```
